question: Can I build a settlement next to another settlement?
expected: No. All three adjacent intersections must be vacant, including your own settlements or cities.
actual_message: No. You must observe the Distance Rule, which states you may only build a settlement on an unoccupied intersection if none of the 3 adjacent intersections contain a settlement or city. This applies to all settlements, including your own.

expected: No. Only players holding more than seven resource cards discard half, rounded down.
actual_message: No, you do not need to discard any cards. The rules state that only players with more than 7 resource cards (8 or more) must discard half of them. Since you hold exactly seven, you are below the threshold and keep all your cards.

question: How many resource cards does a city receive when its adjacent terrain hex produces?
expected: Two of the resource produced by that hex, subject to normal supply rules.
actual_message: A city receives 2 resource cards for each adjacent terrain hex that produces resources. This is double the amount a settlement receives (1 card). The specific type of resource depends on the terrain hex (e.g., brick from hills, lumber from forest). If multiple adjacent hexes produce on the same roll, the city collects 2 cards for each of those hexes.

question: When my shipping route reaches a new island, may I build a settlement there, and what exact distance restriction applies?
expected: A connected shipping route can permit a new coastal settlement; all three neighbouring intersections must still be vacant.
actual_message: Yes, you may build a settlement on a new island if your shipping route reaches its coastline. You must obey the standard Distance Rule: you can only build at an intersection if all three adjacent intersections are vacant (occupied by no settlements or cities). Additionally, the settlement must connect to your network of roads and shipping routes.

question: What happens when an outbreak occurs?
expected: Advance the outbreak marker and add a matching cube to connected cities; resolve chain reactions. Do not outbreak a city again while resolving the current Infection card; do not broaden this to the entire infection step.
actual_message: When an outbreak occurs, move the outbreaks marker forward 1 space. Then, place 1 cube of the disease color on every city connected to the outbreak city. If a connected city already has 3 cubes of that color, do not place a 4th cube; instead, a chain reaction outbreak occurs there after the current one resolves. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to cities that have already had an outbreak while resolving the current Infection card. A city may hold up to 3 cubes of each color. If the outbreaks marker reaches the last space, the game ends and players lose.
